NoteNlpAccessor::mask_numbers¶

Back to Note NLP Accessor API Reference

Signature¶

Note NoteNlpAccessor::mask_numbers() const

Collapse Numeric Runs Into One Semantic Marker¶

mask_numbers() replaces each ASCII numeric run with [NUM]. A run begins at an ASCII digit and continues across digits plus a restricted separator when that separator is immediately followed by another digit.

Byte inside a run

Rule

0 through 9

Always continues the current run.

, . - / : _

Continues only when the next byte is a digit.

Sign, whitespace, letter, or other punctuation

Ends the run or remains outside it.

Consequently 1,234.50, 2024-01-02, 3:45, and 6_000 each become one placeholder. In +7, the plus sign remains and only 7 becomes [NUM]. 1..2 contains two runs because the first dot is not followed by a digit. Digits embedded in x7y are still masked; this method does not require word boundaries.

This broad behavior is appropriate for removing quantities and identifiers. When semantic categories matter, run the narrower currency, date, and time maskers first, or use mask_pii, whose precedence does that automatically. The method recognizes ASCII digits only.

The result is a fresh, shape-identical Text Note. Existing [NUM] markers are unchanged, so repeated application is idempotent. The receiver is not mutated. A digit precheck makes no-number cells a cheap copy path.

Example 1: Whole Numeric Runs¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"IDs 42, 1,234.50, 2024-01-02, +7 and none"})
        .nlp().mask_numbers()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["IDs [NUM], [NUM], [NUM], +[NUM] and none"]

Example 2: Separator And Word Boundaries¶

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::note::make({"1/2 3:45 6_000 8-9; 1..2 and x7y"})
        .nlp().mask_numbers()) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[1], dim=1, numel=1, encoding=utf8)
["[NUM] [NUM] [NUM] [NUM]; [NUM]..[NUM] and x[NUM]y"]

Example 3: Empty, Undefined, And Non-Text Dtypes¶

const auto empty = pluss::note::make(std::vector<std::string>{})
                       .nlp().mask_numbers();
std::cout << "numbers empty dim=" << empty.dim()
          << " numel=" << empty.numel() << '\n';
std::cout << "numbers undefined=" << std::boolalpha
          << pluss::Note::undefined().nlp().mask_numbers().defined() << '\n';
try {
  (void)pluss::note::bytes(
      std::vector<std::string>{"42"}, std::array<std::int64_t, 1>{1})
      .nlp().mask_numbers();
} catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << "numbers Bytes: rejected\n"; }

Output¶

numbers empty dim=1 numel=0
numbers undefined=false
numbers Bytes: rejected

Bool, Int64, and Float64 Notes reject for the same reason: this is a text rewriter, not numeric formatting or arithmetic.

See Also¶

  • mask_currency: preserve monetary category before broad number masking.

  • mask_dates: recognize complete date-shaped spans.

  • mask_times: recognize valid clock-shaped spans.
